'''''Bidens tripartita''''' is a common and widespread species of flowering plant in the sunflower family, [[Asteraceae]], commonly known as '''three-lobe beggarticks''',<ref>{{cite book |editor1-last=Lee |editor1-first=Sangtae |editor2-last=Chang |editor2-first=Kae Sun |title=English Names for Korean Native Plants |year=2015 |publisher=[[Korea National Arboretum]] |location=Pocheon |isbn=978-89-97450-98-5 |page=374 |url=http://www.forest.go.kr/kna/special/download/English_Names_for_Korean_Native_Plants.pdf |access-date=7 March 2019 |via=[[Korea Forest Service]]}}</ref> '''three-part beggarticks''', '''leafy-bracted beggarticks''' or '''trifid bur-marigold'''. It is native to much of [[Eurasia]], [[North Africa]], and [[North America]], with naturalized populations in [[Australia]] and on some [[Pacific Islands]].<ref name=":0">{{GRIN | accessdate = 1 January 2018}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{cite web | url = http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=200023540 | title = ''Bidens tripartita'' Linnaeus | work = [[Flora of North America]]}}</ref><ref name=":2">[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200023540 Flora of China, <big>狼杷草</big> lang pa cao, ''Bidens tripartita'' Linnaeus, Sp. Pl. 2: 831. 1753]</ref><ref name=":3">[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=bidens+tripartita Altervist Flora Italiana, Forbicina comune, ''Bidens tripartita'' L.] includes photos, drawings, European distribution map</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite web |url=http://bie.ala.org.au/species/urn:lsid:biodiversity.org.au:apni.taxon:565681#tab_gallery |title=Atlas of Living Australia |access-date=2015-05-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160331123118/http://bie.ala.org.au/species/urn:lsid:biodiversity.org.au:apni.taxon:565681#tab_gallery |archive-date=2016-03-31 }}</ref>

== Distribution and abundance ==
''Bidens tripartita'' is native to much of [[Eurasia]], [[North Africa]], and [[North America]], with naturalized populations in [[Australia]] and on some [[Pacific Islands]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4" /> ''Bidens tripartita'' is considered relatively rare in southwestern [[British Columbia]] and was likely introduced from eastern [[North America]] and [[Europe]].<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=E-Flora BC Atlas Page |url=https://linnet.geog.ubc.ca/Atlas/Atlas.aspx?sciname=Bidens+tripartita |access-date=2022-12-11 |website=linnet.geog.ubc.ca}}</ref>

== Morphology ==
''Bidens tripartita'' is an annual species with rigid stems and fibrous roots, with a typical [[Habit (biology)|habit]] measuring 20-100 centimeters tall. Leaves are often deeply lobed. Flower heads are discoid and lacking [[ray flowers]]. Fruits are [[Achene|achenes]].<ref name=":5" />

== Uses ==

=== Medicinal ===
Although rarely used for medicinal purposes nowadays, it was once highly esteemed for being effective at staunching blood flow and as a remedy for bleeding, specifically one caused by ruptured blood vessels, but also extending to uterine bleeding and conditions that lead to [[hematuria]].<ref>{{Cite book|title=The encyclopedia of medicinal plants|publisher=DK Pub. ; Distributed by Houghton Mifflin|date=1996|location=New York : Boston|isbn=978-0-7894-1067-2|first=Andrew|last=Chevallier|publication-date=1996|pages=177}}</ref>The species is also known for its styptic, astringent<ref>{{Cite book|title=The dictionary of modern herbalism: a comprehensive guide to practical herbal therapy|publisher=Healing Arts Press ; Distributed in the U.S. by Harper and Row|date=1988|location=Rochester, Vt. : [New York]|isbn=978-0-89281-238-7|first=Simon|last=Mills|pages=48}}</ref>, antiseptic, aperient and diaphoretic<ref name=":6">{{Cite book|title=The new holistic herbal : a herbal celebrating the wholeness of life|last=Hoffmann|first=David|publisher=Longmead, Shaftesbury, Dorset [England] : Element Books|year=1990|isbn=9781852301934|pages=186}}</ref> effects on the human body. Remedies containing the herb usually take form of tinctures and infusions.

=== Other ===
The dried herb, specifically the dried flower heads, of ''Bidens tripartita'' can be burnt to release a [[Cedar (plant)|cedar]]-like smell that may be used for an incense against insects.<ref name=":6" />
